instructions: Read the original passage and choose one answer for each question.
passage:
In the fictional town of Fairbrook, neighbors have agreed to care for a small shared garden. There are four raised beds beside the community room. The group will meet on Sunday at ten to decide what to put in each bed. Hana has never grown anything before, so she asks Arun to explain the plan in simple language. He says nobody needs special experience to join; people can start by watching and asking questions. At the meeting, members will write down which jobs each person wants to try. A sign at the entrance will say that visitors may join the discussion even if they do not plan to plant anything.

One bed will hold a mix of flowers. Arun shows Hana a seed and explains that the group will sow seeds in rows. A seed needs suitable conditions to sprout. As a young plant begins to grow, its root stays in the earth and its stem rises above it. A leaf can be a different shape from a flower's petal. Later, a blossom may open on a branch. Hana writes these words on small cards, but she will not attach the cards to the plants.

Another bed is for a herb collection. The group has chosen mint, basil and parsley because members want to use small amounts in a shared meal. The mint will stay in a pot beside the bed, and the basil will go in the sunnier strip. Arun explains that the place gets morning sunlight and afternoon shade. The group will look at the garden notice before deciding where to put the parsley. They do not assume that every plant needs the same place.

The third bed is for a crop that the group hopes to share at a later harvest. Members will discuss the choice rather than promise an exact amount. A neighbor plans to bring compost on Friday. The group has not bought fertilizer; it will first read the instructions on any product it considers and ask the garden staff about the local rules. The fourth bed will remain empty until the next meeting, so people who arrive later can help decide how to use it.

The tools are kept in a locked room. Hana will bring a bucket to the first meeting, and Arun will check that the shovel and rake are returned afterward. A hose is available, but it must not block the path. During a visit, Hana notices an insect on a flower and a butterfly near the fence. She also sees a bee by the herbs. Arun suggests watching from a little distance and leaving the creatures undisturbed. If heavy rain begins on Sunday, the group will discuss its plan indoors instead of working in the beds.
